# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection

**Capture:** 2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap | **LAN:** 10.2.28.0/24, domain `easyas123.tech` / workgroup `mshome.net`

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR |
| Logged-in user | brolf (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, frames to/from 10.2.28.2, the domain controller EASYAS123-DC) |

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** TCP stream 40 (10.2.28.88:51912 → 45.131.214.85:443) shows plaintext HTTP carrying the literal NetSupport Manager client/gateway protocol:
- Requests: `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, `POST /fakeurl.htm`, body `CMD=POLL` / `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>`
- Responses: `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`, `CMD=ENCD` replies

`/fakeurl.htm` as the POST target combined with the `NetSupport Manager/1.3` UA and `NetSupport Gateway/1.92` server banner is the documented C2 fingerprint for this RAT family, not inferred from behavior alone.

## Suspected Delivery
At t=44.4s the host resolved and browsed `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (TLS SNI, resolved to Akamai IP 23.64.147.24) immediately before, at t=44.7s, resolving the malicious domain `vadusa.xyz`. This sequencing is consistent with a fake-CAPTCHA/"ClickFix" lure page impersonating a DOT/FMCSA compliance site tricking the user into executing a clipboard-pasted command that fetched the RAT. No malware executable was observed transferred over HTTP in this capture (all `.exe`/binary HTTP objects recovered are legitimate Windows Delivery Optimization and Adobe update payloads — see benign context); the loader/installer stage was not captured, likely delivered over an encrypted channel or before/outside the capture window.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `45.131.214.85:443` — NetSupport RAT gateway; plaintext HTTP (not TLS) despite port 443. 264 `POST /fakeurl.htm` beacons observed from t=45s to t=15,682s (~4h21m), stream 40.

**Malicious domain**
- `vadusa.xyz` — resolves to 45.131.214.85 (DNS A record, frames at t=44.77s/44.81s)

**Malicious URL**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — C2 poll/data-exchange endpoint (all 264 requests)

**File names / hashes**
- None recoverable. No dropper/payload executable was captured in cleartext HTTP; all encrypted RAT traffic (`CMD=ENCD` blobs) cannot be hashed without the session key.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
- `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (23.64.147.24) — legitimate Akamai-hosted US DOT site, browsed as apparent lure but the domain itself is not malicious infrastructure.
- `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `acroipm2.adobe.com`, `ocsp.digicert.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `*.msn.com`, `www.bing.com`, `services.gfe.nvidia.com`, `update.googleapis.com` — routine OS/CDN/update/telemetry traffic, including the "PE32/DOS executable" and "Chrome extension" file-typed HTTP objects, which are Windows Delivery Optimization chunks, not malware.

## Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as domain user `brolf`, was compromised with NetSupport RAT after browsing a DOT/FMCSA-themed lure that led to `vadusa.xyz`. The RAT established persistent encrypted C2 over plaintext HTTP on port 443 to 45.131.214.85, identified unambiguously by its native NetSupport Manager/Gateway protocol headers, beaconing roughly 264 times over 4+ hours.
